$comment: Canonical authority policy for #93. This file is DATA, not prose: it states who may authorize
what, and it lists the exact normalized sentences that are permitted to make an authority claim
on a canonical surface. test/governance-model.test.js enforces both halves.
Why it exists: five consecutive review rounds found bypasses in a prose scanner built from
regexes. Each fix narrowed a window and the next round found another way in, because detecting
bad prose is an unbounded problem. This inverts it — only known-good statements are permitted,
and anything else fails until a human adds it here deliberately. That is the same discipline as
the closed nine-key execution-gate schema, applied to documentation.
The allowlist is a BASELINE of text already reviewed across rounds 1-13. Its value is not that each
line was re-derived from first principles, but that any FUTURE change to a sentence naming a
governed document fails the suite until a human puts it here on purpose.
